context.note: TEST-DESIGNER performed the full 10-AC gap-check against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-194 acceptance criteria, cross-referencing every criterion against the actual test files (read in full) and the shipped moduledocs (read in full), not just against ELIXIR-DEV's own step-02a handoff claims. Full rationale, AC-by-AC verdict table, and verification transcript in handoffs/WF02-REQ194-20260830/test-designer-gap-analysis.md. Summary: AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC7/AC10 were already genuinely covered by ELIXIR-DEV's initial 53 tests -- confirmed by reading the assertions, not assumed. AC8's grep-based test correctly and deliberately excludes lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex (design doc section 5/6 and registry.ex's own moduledoc both state explicitly that family #1, active_instances, is NOT telemetry-driven -- Poller calls the Registry module directly by design, so requiring poller.ex to avoid referencing Letflow.Metrics.Registry would contradict the design, not fill a gap). Two real gaps were found and fixed, both in test/letflow/routers/metrics_exposition_test.exs: (1) AC6's adversarial cross-tenant scan previously checked tenant_id/definition_id/instance_id/schema_name (8 identifiers across 2 tenants) but never task_id or actor_id, even though design section 1 and both moduledocs name all five identifier classes (tenant_id, definition_id, instance_id, task_id, actor_id) as forbidden label values -- complete_one_task!/1 now captures and returns task_id plus two distinct actor_id values (one for Engine.create/2, one for Engine.complete_task/3) and the AC6 test now scans for all 14 identifiers; (2) AC9 previously confirmed Letflow.Routers.Metrics no longer loads and GET /health still works, but never checked what happens to REQ-078's actual retired path, GET /api/v1/metrics -- added a test confirming it is rejected (measured directly: real unauthenticated request returns 401 from Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline's step-1 short-circuit, before the absent /metrics forward entry could even be reached) and never serves the old {instances,tasks,definitions} JSON shape (confirmed against git history of the deleted lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex). Both new/modified tests were run for real against the shipped implementation in this environment (toolchain via asdf + live Postgres both available): mix compile --warnings-as-errors is clean; the full metrics-area test run (test/letflow/metrics/, test/letflow/routers/metrics_exposition_test.exs, test/letflow/plugs/http_metrics_test.exs, test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs, test/letflow/routers/req078_supporting_routes_test.exs) reports 54 passed (the prior 53 plus one net-new test case; the AC6 widening modified an existing test in place). No existing assertion was weakened, removed, or had its expected value changed. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR should independently re-derive AC-to-test traceability (not trust this note), and in particular verify: (a) the AC8 poller.ex exclusion really is design-sanctioned and not TEST-DESIGNER rationalizing a gap away -- read design doc section 5/6 and registry.ex's moduledoc directly; (b) the AC6 widened identifier list actually would fail if a label leak were reintroduced (it is an additive assertion over a real scrape body of real seeded data, not a tautology); (c) AC9's new test's 401/404 branching is honestly justified by the real AuthPipeline plug order, not a loophole that would also pass if the old endpoint were still silently reachable.
